# Foundry VTT Module Architecture

**Purpose**: Complete documentation of the `foundry/` module pipeline — how Ikuisuus content is exported, transformed, token-generated, and compiled into Foundry VTT compendium packs.

## Overview

The `foundry/` directory contains the `ikuisuus-damocles` Foundry VTT module. It exports Damocles content (monsters, heirlooms, spells, trinkets) from the Library of Ikuisuus into dnd5e-compatible compendium packs that can be installed in Foundry VTT v12+.

### Quick Start

```bash
# Full pipeline (export → token generation → pack compilation)
npm run foundry:build

# Individual stages
npm run foundry:export  # Export JSON source files only
npm run foundry:pack    # Compile LevelDB packs only
```

## Module Structure

```
foundry/
  module.json              ← Foundry module manifest
  tsconfig.json            ← TypeScript config (extends root tsconfig.scripts.json)
  assets/
    frames/
      frame.png            ← Token circle frame overlay (256×256)
    images/                ← Bundled portrait WebPs (copied from public/library/)
    tokens/                ← Generated circular token images
  packs/
    _source/
      monsters/            ← JSON source for Actor compendium (one file per actor)
      heirlooms/           ← JSON source for heirloom Item compendium
      spells/              ← JSON source for spell Item compendium
      trinkets/            ← JSON source for trinket Item compendium
    monsters/              ← Compiled LevelDB pack (git-committed)
    heirlooms/             ← Compiled LevelDB pack (git-committed)
    spells/                ← Compiled LevelDB pack (git-committed)
    trinkets/              ← Compiled LevelDB pack (git-committed)
  scripts/
    export.ts              ← Main export orchestrator
    constants/
      dnd5eMaps.ts         ← Lookup tables (sizes, damage types, conditions, skills, languages)
    transformers/
      monsterTransformer.ts ← MonsterMetadata → dnd5e NPC Actor
    utils/
      idGenerator.ts       ← Deterministic 16-char Foundry IDs from slugs
      mdxToHtml.ts         ← MDX content → clean HTML for biography fields
      traitParsers.ts      ← Trait string arrays → dnd5e trait objects
```

## Module Manifest (`module.json`)

The manifest declares four compendium packs under the module ID `ikuisuus-damocles`:

| Pack name   | Label              | Document type | dnd5e system |
| ----------- | ------------------ | ------------- | ------------ |
| `monsters`  | Damocles Monsters  | `Actor`       | dnd5e        |
| `heirlooms` | Damocles Heirlooms | `Item`        | dnd5e        |
| `spells`    | Damocles Spells    | `Item`        | dnd5e        |
| `trinkets`  | Damocles Trinkets  | `Item`        | dnd5e        |

All packs are grouped under a `Damocles` packFolder for cleaner in-game presentation.

**Compatibility**: Foundry VTT minimum v12, verified v13. System: dnd5e ≥ 3.0.0.

## Export Pipeline

### Data Flow

```
.meta/en/monsters/*.metadata.json   (pg backend — preferred)
               ↓  (falls back to)
src/content/en/monsters/*.metadata.json
               +
src/content/en/monsters/*.sheet.mdx
               ↓
   foundry/scripts/export.ts
               ↓
  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  monsterTransformer.ts  → Actor JSON            │
  │  mdxToHtml.ts           → biography HTML        │
  │  idGenerator.ts         → deterministic _id     │
  │  traitParsers.ts        → trait value/custom    │
  └────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
               ↓
 foundry/packs/_source/monsters/{id}.json
               +
 foundry/assets/images/{portrait}.webp  (bundled)
 foundry/assets/tokens/{portrait}.token.webp  (generated)
               ↓
    foundry:pack  (@foundryvtt/foundryvtt-cli)
               ↓
 foundry/packs/monsters/  (LevelDB)
```

### Stage 1: Metadata Discovery (`discoverMetadataFiles`)

The orchestrator first checks `.meta/en/monsters/` for files generated by the PostgreSQL backend (runtime metadata extraction). If none exist, it falls back to source-adjacent `.metadata.json` files in `src/content/en/monsters/`.

This dual-source strategy ensures the export works both offline (using build-time metadata) and in the full stack environment where the pg backend pre-populates `.meta/`.

```
.meta/en/monsters/rotworm.metadata.json    ← preferred (pg backend)
src/content/en/monsters/rotworm.metadata.json  ← fallback (build-time)
```

### Stage 2: Monster Transformation

Each `.metadata.json` file may contain one or more `MonsterMetadata` records (arrays for multi-variant files, e.g., Albedo and her lair form). Every record produces exactly one NPC Actor JSON document.

**Multi-variant files**: When a single `.sheet.mdx` contains multiple stat blocks (e.g., a boss and lair variant), the metadata array has multiple entries distinguished by `subSlug`. Example: `albedo.metadata.json` produces two actors — one keyed by `"albedo-the-bleak-bloom"` and one by `"albedo-lair-form"`.

### Stage 3: Image Bundling (`bundleImages`)

Portrait images referenced in metadata (e.g., `"/library/images/Albedo.webp"`) are copied from `public/library/images/` to `foundry/assets/images/`. Image paths in the Actor JSON are rewritten from the Next.js public path to the module-relative path:

```
/library/images/Albedo.webp
  → modules/ikuisuus-damocles/assets/images/Albedo.webp
```

Biography HTML also has its image paths rewritten by `rewriteBiographyImages()` for the same reason.

### Stage 4: Token Generation (`generateTokens`)

Circular token images are generated from portraits using Sharp:

1. **Crop** — Extract a center-biased square from the portrait (top offset 15% to favor the face region)
2. **Resize** — Scale to 256×256 pixels
3. **Background fill** — Composite over `#28303b` dark background to fill transparent areas
4. **Circular mask** — Apply SVG circle mask (radius 95% of half-dimension to leave a thin border)
5. **Frame overlay** — Composite `foundry/assets/frames/frame.png` on top
6. **Convert** — Output as WebP at 90% quality

The default token (`_default.token.webp`) is generated for monsters without a portrait image: just the background color + frame.

Token filenames map 1:1 to portrait filenames with the `.token.webp` suffix:

```
Albedo.webp → Albedo.token.webp
```

The second export pass (after token generation) writes `prototypeToken.texture.src` back into each Actor JSON, pointing to the module token path.

### Stage 5: Pack Compilation (`foundry:pack`)

`@foundryvtt/foundryvtt-cli`'s `compilePack()` reads all JSON files from `foundry/packs/_source/{pack}/` and compiles them into a LevelDB database at `foundry/packs/{pack}/`. The compiled packs are committed to git and distributed with the module.

**Known benign warning**: LevelDB sometimes emits a `LEVEL_ITERATOR_NOT_OPEN` error on completion; the build script treats this as non-fatal because the pack data is written successfully before the error occurs.

## Key Utilities

### `idGenerator.ts` — Deterministic IDs

Foundry VTT document IDs must be exactly 16 characters, alphanumeric. The exporter generates stable IDs by SHA-256 hashing the content slug (namespaced with the content type), then mapping hash bytes to the alphanumeric alphabet:

```typescript
generateFoundryId('rotworm', 'monster');
// Always returns the same 16-char string for this input
// e.g. "K47nshT30O5SXUBC"
```

The namespace prevents collisions between a monster and an item with the same slug. **This determinism is critical**: running `foundry:build` multiple times must not produce different IDs, so Foundry compendium entries stay stable across module updates and GMs don't lose actor links.

### `mdxToHtml.ts` — MDX → Biography HTML

Biography HTML for Foundry actor/item description fields is generated by running the MDX source through the same `next-mdx-remote-client/rsc` `evaluate()` pipeline used by the main app. Custom components are handled as follows:

| Component                                              | Treatment                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `BlendedImage`, `Image`                                | Rendered as plain `<img>` with `src`/`alt` forwarded |
| `MonsterTable`, `HeirloomTable`, `SpellTable`, etc.    | `Noop` — silently dropped                            |
| `Collapsible`, `FlexRenderer`, `HorizontalSplit`, etc. | `PassThrough` — children rendered                    |
| `table` (markdown)                                     | Rendered as plain `<table>` element                  |
| `ClearFloats`, `ParallaxBackdrop`, `Tooltip`           | `Noop`                                               |

`extractMonsterDescription()` strips the stat block header (everything before the first `\n---\n` separator in the MDX) and renders only the traits, actions, and narrative content as HTML.

### `traitParsers.ts` — Trait Normalization

Three parsers convert metadata trait string arrays to dnd5e trait objects:

```typescript
interface ParsedTrait {
  value: string[]; // Recognized dnd5e keys
  custom: string; // Semicolon-joined unrecognized entries
}

parseDamageTraits(['fire', 'cold', 'Solar Flare']);
// → { value: ['fire', 'cold'], custom: 'Solar Flare' }

parseConditionTraits(['Terrified', 'poisoned']);
// → { value: ['frightened', 'poisoned'], custom: '' }
// Note: "Terrified" maps to dnd5e "frightened"

parseLanguages(['common', 'Voidtongue']);
// → { value: ['common'], custom: 'Voidtongue' }
```

### `dnd5eMaps.ts` — Lookup Tables

All string-to-dnd5e-key mappings live here as exported `Record<string, string>` constants:

| Map                 | Purpose                                                    |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `SIZE_MAP`          | `"gargantuan"` → `"grg"`, `"large"` → `"lg"`, etc.         |
| `TOKEN_SIZE_MAP`    | `"gargantuan"` → `4` (grid squares), `"large"` → `2`, etc. |
| `DAMAGE_TYPE_MAP`   | `"fire"` → `"fire"`, 13 standard damage types              |
| `CONDITION_MAP`     | `"terrified"` → `"frightened"` + all standard conditions   |
| `SKILL_MAP`         | `"perception"` → `"prc"`, all 18 skills                    |
| `SKILL_ABILITY_MAP` | `"prc"` → `"wis"`, maps skills to their governing ability  |
| `LANGUAGE_MAP`      | `"common"` → `"common"`, 16 standard languages             |

Custom Damocles conditions or damage types not in these maps land in the `custom` string field of the trait object (visible in Foundry as free-text).

## Monster Transformer Deep Dive

`monsterTransformer.ts` maps `MonsterMetadata` → `FoundryNpcActor`. Key mapping logic:

### Ability Scores

```typescript
system.abilities.str.value = monster.abilities?.str?.score ?? 10;
system.abilities.str.proficient =
  monster.savingThrows?.str !== undefined ? 1 : 0;
```

Saving throw proficiency is detected by the presence of the key in `savingThrows` (not the value), which reflects how the metadata is parsed from stat block tables.

### Skills

Skill entries from metadata look like `"Perception +15"`. The transformer:

1. Parses the skill name and bonus with a regex
2. Looks up the dnd5e skill key (`prc`) and governing ability (`wis`)
3. Derives the ability modifier from the score
4. Computes the proficiency multiplier: `bonus - abilityMod` compared to `prof` and `prof×2`
   - ≥ `prof×2` → expertise (multiplier `2`)
   - ≥ `prof` → proficient (multiplier `1`)
   - ≥ `floor(prof/2)` → half-proficient (multiplier `0.5`)
   - otherwise → non-proficient (multiplier `0`)

### AC Calculation

All AC is stored as a flat override (`calc: 'flat'`). This is a deliberate simplification; dnd5e's auto-calculated AC types require knowing equipped items, and NPCs only need the flat value from their stat block.

### Token Dimensions

`prototypeToken.width` and `prototypeToken.height` are set from `TOKEN_SIZE_MAP` to the correct grid-square dimensions for the creature's size (e.g., Huge = 3×3, Large = 2×2).

## Adding New Content Types

The current export only covers monsters. Heirlooms, spells, and trinkets are planned (Phase 3 in the original design). To add a new content type:

1. **Create a transformer** in `foundry/scripts/transformers/`:

   ```typescript
   // heirloomTransformer.ts
   export async function transformHeirloom(
     heirloom: HeirloomMetadata,
     mdxContent: string,
   ): Promise<FoundryItemDocument> {
     /* ... */
   }
   ```

2. **Add export logic** to `export.ts` — a new function parallel to `exportMonsters()` that:
   - Discovers metadata files from `.meta/en/{type}/` or `src/content/en/{type}/`
   - Calls the transformer
   - Writes to `foundry/packs/_source/{type}/{id}.json`

3. **Verify `module.json`** already declares the pack (it does for heirlooms, spells, trinkets).

4. **Run `foundry:build`** and verify the new pack compiles.

## TypeScript Configuration

`foundry/tsconfig.json` extends `tsconfig.scripts.json` at the root, with:

- `rootDir: ".."` — so imports can reach `src/` from `foundry/scripts/`
- Path alias `@/*` → `../src/*`
- Explicit `include: ["scripts/**/*.ts", "../src/lib/db/content/schemas/**/*.ts"]`

This allows transformer files to import `MonsterMetadata` directly from the canonical schema in `src/lib/db/content/schemas/monsterMetadata.ts` without duplicating type definitions.

## Metadata Source Strategy

The exporter uses a **preference-with-fallback** pattern for metadata discovery:

```
Prefer:   .meta/en/monsters/*.metadata.json   (pg backend runtime)
Fallback: src/content/en/monsters/*.metadata.json  (build-time static)
```

This makes the pipeline portable:

- **Full stack** (postgres running): `.meta/` has the freshest data from the pg content adapter
- **Offline / CI**: Falls back to the static `.metadata.json` files generated by `npm run generate-metadata`

## Error Handling

The export loop uses individual `try/catch` per metadata file. Failed files write to stderr and increment an error counter but don't abort the batch. If any errors occur, the process exits with code 1 after completing all files — allowing partial exports to still produce packs while signaling CI failure.

Token generation failures are non-fatal (warnings only) — the default token is used as a fallback.

## NPM Scripts

| Script                   | Effect                                                                                 |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `npm run foundry:export` | Run `export.ts` via tsx — produces `_source/` JSON + bundles images + generates tokens |
| `npm run foundry:pack`   | Compile `_source/` to LevelDB packs via `@foundryvtt/foundryvtt-cli`                   |
| `npm run foundry:build`  | `foundry:export && foundry:pack` — full pipeline                                       |
